instrument_defects_this_measurement_foun: A relative interpreter path was resolved with Path.resolve(), which followed the virtualenv symlink into the base interpreter; every suite then reported 'No module named pytest'.
The trace hook was named pytest_session_finished, which pytest does not know; the suite ran, passed, and wrote no trace -- indistinguishable from 'the module was never called'.

reduce_module() kept only the functions under test, so a function that called a helper raised NameError and every law about it reported NOT_APPLICABLE: silence that reads exactly like 'this code has no laws'.

Keeping definitions then made whole modules unloadable when a kept definition named something the reduction dropped; 43 of 121 modules failed to load, and a module that fails to load produces no laws at all. _load_module now falls back to statement-by-statement loading and records what could not be defined.
A candidate whose changed definition could not be defined in the reduction is reported UNVERIFIABLE (CANDIDATE_NOT_LOADABLE_UNDER_REDUCTION), never as a survivor and never as a law kill.

The law grid was invented (small ints, short strings), which cannot call a function that takes a parsed record. The grid can now be the arguments the real suite itself passed, captured by tracing its execution.

real_geometry.source: paths, source lines and identifier lists read from the corpus roots

reading.what_a_pass_is_worth_here: 0.8021 of behaviour-altering candidates were rejected by the paired real suite; per pair the rate ranged from 1/6 (skill_recheck_v1) to 6/6 (six pairs). A pass is therefore a coverage certificate of real but unequal strength, not a correctness proof.
reading.what_this_does_not_show: That a verifier is impossible. It shows that a verifier made of the relations a program's own SHAPE suggests is worth 0 on top of a real suite, and that what would add information is a relation that names what the code MEANS.
why_the_law_adds_zero: The only law kind that confirms widely on real code is TOTALITY ('it ran'): 71 of 120 proposed on the invented grid, 51 of 120 on the suite's own arguments. On the very arguments a suite already executed, a passing suite has already certified it.

The informative kinds are refuted by the code itself (INVOLUTION 20 refuted, IDEMPOTENCE 7, COMMUTATIVITY 3 of 42). An invented relation about real code is usually false, and knowing which relation is true of a program is knowledge, not shape.

Structure-derived laws address top-level functions; in this tree much of the behaviour lives in methods (the mutation engine produced e.g. `Localization.localized`), which no law in this vocabulary can address.

Even with a confirmed law pointed at the mutated function (19 of 19 survivors), the law did not fire: the behaviour the mutation changed was invisible on the inputs it was confirmed on. That is identifiability, in the small, measured rather than argued.

what_this_is: A producer-run measurement, on this repository's own code and its own unedited test files, of two quantities: (1) of behaviour-altering candidates a real suite ACCEPTS, how many are actually wrong; (2) of those the suite accepts, how many a law confirmed on the pristine module can still reject, with a witness.
what_this_is_not: Not a proof of correctness, not a benchmark score, not independent verification. ACCEPTED_BY_BOTH means nothing available falsified the candidate. A kill is not a proof and a survivor is not an approval. truth.achieved remains false.
